title: Functions and Means of Accretive Operators
summary: Let $A$ be a bounded accretive operator on a Hilbert space and $f(t)$ an operator monotone function on $(0, \infty)$ with $f(0)>-\infty$. Then, for $ε>0$, analytic function $f (A+εI) $ is defined by Riesz-Dunford integral. We define $f(A)$ as the norm limit of it and show $$ f(A) = f(0)I + b A + \int_0^{\infty} (\frac{1}λ I - (λI + A)^{-1}) dμ(λ).$$ This is a generalization of fractional powers $$A^r = \frac{\sin r π}π \int_0^{\infty} (\frac{1}λ I - (λI + A)^{-1}) λ^{r} dλ\quad (0<r<1).$$ Let $A$ and $B$ be strictly accretive matrices, namely those real parts are positive definite.
